issues.legal_issue: A representative suit against the Government is not defective merely because more than one person served the statutory notice but only one of them later sued, where the suing person served the notice and the suit proceeds with the court’s permission on behalf of persons with the same interest.
material_facts: Two persons served the Government with a notice challenging the notification and stating the cause of action and relief sought on behalf of the affected inamdars.
The respondent, who had served the notice, alone filed the suit more than two months later, seeking the stated relief on behalf of all the inamdars.
The court permitted the respondent to bring the representative suit, and the cause of action and relief in the suit were not different from those set out in the notice.
issues.conclusion: The suit was not defective under section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure merely because the other person who served the notice did not join the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure is imperative and requires strict compliance, but a notice must be reasonably construed in light of its purpose: giving the Government an opportunity to reconsider its legal position. Incidental errors may be ignored where the required information is conveyed. Order 1, rule 8 permits one or more persons with a common interest to sue representatively with the court’s permission; those represented do not thereby become plaintiffs. The identity requirement discussed in Vellayan Chettiar v. Government of the Province of Madras and Government of the Province of Bombay v. Pestonji Ardeshir Wadia did not make this suit defective, because the person who sued had himself served the notice and the suit was representative, on the same cause of action and for the same relief.

rule.if: suit_against_government and statutory_notice_served and notice_served_by_suing_person and notice_identifies_suing_person and notice_states_cause_and_relief and suit_filed_after_waiting_period and representative_suit_permitted and another_notice_giver_did_not_join_suit

predicates.suit_against_government: The proceeding is a suit brought against the Government.
predicates.statutory_notice_served: A written notice of the proposed suit was delivered to the appropriate government authority.
predicates.notice_served_by_suing_person: The person who later brought the suit had also served the notice.
predicates.notice_identifies_suing_person: The notice gave identifying details of the person who later brought the suit.
predicates.notice_states_cause_and_relief: The notice stated the cause of action and the relief sought with sufficient particularity.
predicates.suit_filed_after_waiting_period: The suit was filed after the applicable waiting period following service of the notice.
predicates.representative_suit_permitted: The court permitted the suing person to proceed on behalf of others sharing the same interest.
predicates.another_notice_giver_did_not_join_suit: At least one other person who served the notice did not join as a plaintiff.

issues.definition: When a person who served an adequate notice later brings a permitted representative suit against the Government on the same cause of action and for the same relief, another notice-giver’s failure to join the suit does not make it defective.

issues.legal_issue: Court permission is required to institute a representative suit, not to serve notice of the proposed suit on the Government.
material_facts: The proposed action was a representative suit against the Government following a statutory notice.
The notice was served before the court granted permission to institute the representative suit.
The court later granted permission for the suit to proceed representatively.
issues.conclusion: Permission of the court need not be obtained before serving notice on the Government; it is required for instituting the representative suit.
issues.legal_principle: Order 1, rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the court’s permission to institute a representative suit. Section 80 does not require prior permission to serve a notice, and the Code provides no machinery for obtaining permission to serve such a notice.

predicates.representative_suit_against_government: The proceeding is a proposed representative suit against the Government.
predicates.notice_served_before_permission_for_suit: The proposed suit’s notice was served before the court granted permission to institute the representative suit.

issues.definition: For a proposed representative suit against the Government, serving notice before obtaining permission to institute the suit does not require prior court permission.

issues.legal_issue: Lands do not constitute an estate under the applicable definition when the original grant was not of the entire village and the Government did not confirm or recognize it as such.
material_facts: The original grant concerned certain lands, and the original grant document was not available.
During enfranchisement, only the cultivated area was confirmed; waste, banjar and other uncultivated lands were excluded.
The Zamindar dealt with the excluded waste and banjar lands as its own, including granting jeroyiti pattas, and its title to the tank was recognized.
The documentary evidence supported the finding that the grant was not of the entire village.
issues.conclusion: The lands were not an estate within section 3(2)(d) of the Madras Estates Land Act, 1908, and the Madras Estates Rent Reduction Act, 1947 did not apply to them.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3(2)(d) of the Madras Estates Land Act, 1908, as applied by the Court, the relevant category required a grant of the whole village and confirmation or recognition of that grant by the Government. Because the evidence established a grant of less than the entire village and confirmation of only part of the area, the lands did not meet that definition; accordingly, the Madras Estates Rent Reduction Act, 1947, which had been applied on the basis that the lands were an estate, did not apply. The Court relied on the documentary evidence and the parties’ dealings with the excluded lands; it cited no earlier case as authority for this issue.

rule.if: estate_status_dispute and grant_not_of_entire_village and confirmation_limited_to_part_of_area and (excluded_waste_treated_as_separate_property or zamindar_title_to_excluded_land_recognized)

predicates.estate_status_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether granted lands qualify as an estate for application of rent-reduction legislation.
predicates.grant_not_of_entire_village: The evidence shows that the original grant did not include the entire village.
predicates.confirmation_limited_to_part_of_area: The government confirmation or recognition covered only part of the village area.
predicates.excluded_waste_treated_as_separate_prope: The excluded waste or uncultivated lands were dealt with separately from the granted lands.
predicates.zamindar_title_to_excluded_land_recogniz: The evidence recognized the zamindar’s ownership of lands excluded from the grant.

issues.definition: Where an estate-status dispute concerns a grant short of the whole village and only part of the area was confirmed, evidence that excluded lands remained separate property supports the conclusion that the lands are not an estate and the rent-reduction law does not apply.
